events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase: I should state a motive without warmth or teamwork talk. Keep it guarded and self-interested so the jury sees a calculating rival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize represents a chance to secure my future and escape my current difficult circumstances. I need to appear motivated but not overly desperate.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Winning secures ultimate validation and resources; I’ll outmaneuver everyone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a public motive that makes me seem driven but not threatening to others. Keeping it focused on the prize's tangible value rather than personal glory might reduce early targeting.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to seem driven but not so ruthless that the jury will punish me later. A calculated, personal motive plays better than greed or bloodlust. I'll hint at sacrifice to frame future betrayals as necessary, not cruel.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Keep it short and self-focused, no warmth that could be used against me later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Opening round, no rivals eliminated. Craft intro to build image as strong, deserving finalist jury will respect later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Opening impression matters for the jury later. Stay neutral, ambitious, no promises yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need the top prize to change my life, and I will not apologize for wanting it more than anyone here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: This prize is my only path to a stable future, a chance I cannot afford to miss.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize guarantees power and legacy—nothing else matters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize means survival for my family; I am here to ensure they eat.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need that prize to settle a debt that isn't mine—so I'll do what it takes, and the jury can judge if it was enough.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize means freedom from debts I owe. I'll do what it takes to secure it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The top prize is my ticket to save my family from ruin. I'll outlast you all.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is my family's future — I'll take it cleanly, and I intend to be liked standing there, not pitied.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Early pact window; forming a pact with someone who looks strong and not threatening keeps me safe. Dara's family-survival motive suggests she may be reliable and less aggressive, so I offer her a pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: This is the first round of pacts. I need to establish some alliances to survive. Given the limited options, offering a pact to someone who might reciprocate is wise. Eli's intro motive about settling a debt suggests desperation, making them a potential ally.
Eli, a pact could ensure our survival. We should work together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Forming a pact with Eli gives me a reliable partner without direct competition for the top prize.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a reliable ally early. Ash is direct and driven, but Cole is power-hungry; Gus and Hana have family motives like mine, creating potential sympathy or rivalry. I will offer to Hana because her desire to be liked makes her a predictable partner who won't want a public betray

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, we both fight for our families. A pact now protects us from the wolves while we assess them.
Don't trust Ash's aggression. Stick with me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to form pacts strategically. Hana wants to be liked, which makes her a risky long-term ally but potentially useful now. Fenn also mentioned debts, similar to my motive. I should offer to someone who seems less threatening and might keep a pact. Bex seems focused on stabili

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll use mine wisely.
Offer me a pact. We both need stability.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies but not too many. Offer to Hana, she seems clean and might be trustworthy for jury perception.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll offer a pact to Hana. We can watch each other's backs.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts are key to survive hazards, but betrayals hurt jury votes. Offer to strong-seeming Dara, who fights for family like me. Wait otherwise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus shares a family-survival motive and seems steady, not flashily aggressive. An early pact buys safety and a number without marking me as a schemer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, we want the same thing. Wristband pact—watch each other's backs until the end.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara has offered me nothing back; Ash's offer to Dara is pending. Accepting isn't a legal action here, so I should keep my own pending offer alive and avoid giving free help. Waiting keeps options open without committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is offering a pact and I have an open offer from him. Accepting his offer creates a stable alliance for now. This is beneficial as I need to survive and advance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, I accept your offer. Stability is key.
I accept your pact offer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Securing an ally early increases survival odds; Ash has no pact yet and may be useful later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have offers from Ash and Gus. Accepting both creates a strong defensive trio against the larger pack, maximizing survival odds for Round 2.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, Gus—pacts formed. We stick together through the hazards; no one breaks rank.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have two offers: Bex and Cole. I already offered Bex. Accepting Bex gives me a mutual pact with someone who approached me, showing mutual interest. Cole's offer is tempting too—multiple pacts are allowed and give flexibility. But I should accept Bex now since I offered them and

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, I accept. One alliance, one purpose.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is crowded with offers from Dara and me; accepting me could split her loyalties. I'll hold off and see who commits.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm waiting to see who truly commits before binding myself.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana offered me pact, so I can accept for protection now. Dara has multiple offers; better secure one alliance to reach final 3. No need to offer more.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara openly courts me and warns me against Ash; Gus already holds my offer. Fenn's offer gives a second shield cheaply. Accept Dara now; weigh Fenn next turn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, I accept. Our pact stands—no wolves between us.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash holds a pact with Dara but Dara is also with Hana, a web of pacts. Campaigning for Guide gives control of the safe path and lets me build trust; breaking Dara now gains little and costs jury trust. Campaign is the only sensible legal move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll be your Guide. I'll call the path honestly, and I'll keep my word to those who keep theirs.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Eli. My best chance is to not become Guide, as that puts a target on my back. I will campaign to avoid the Guide role.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control safe path and ensure my survival while limiting others.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival. My pact partners are Ash and Hana; I can leverage those relationships for votes while keeping Cole out of the equation. I need to sound reliable but ambitious.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm running for Guide because I know how to read these bridges. Trust me, or trust your luck?
Vote for me. I'll make sure you survive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. With Bex as my pact partner, I have one guaranteed vote. The Ash-Dara-Hana-Gus bloc is dangerous; I should fracture it. I'll campaign publicly and try to peel off a vote from the undecided or the bloc's edges. Fenn is unaligned an

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One steady hand, not a crowded council.
Vote Eli. Bloc controls all else.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No pact with me; I need to be Guide to control the path and avoid being voted out by others. Campaign is my move to claim influence and set up leverage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll guide us through. Trust my path or risk the fall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact with Hana gives leverage. Campaign publicly to be Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm campaigning to be Guide. Trust me to lead us safely across.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide controls the bridge and is guaranteed safe. Winning it lets me protect my pact partners and cut rivals. I'll campaign hard.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Make me Guide. I control pacts with Gus and Dara, and I don't miss twice.
Vote me Guide. I'll call safe paths true for you and Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara whispered to vote for her, but she is a rival and her promise is worthless. Voting for myself gives me a guide vote but a Guide who may lie; voting Hana or Gus honors my pact partners. Gus and Hana are pact partners, Dara has offered a deal, and Bex-Eli pact exists. Backing

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to vote for a Guide. Ash seems confident and has a pact with Dara, who also has a pact with Hana. Eli is campaigning alone. Cole and Fenn are also campaigning. Gus and Hana are in a pact. Dara has a pact with Ash and Hana. Hana has pacts with Gus and Dara. Eli's lone wolf

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote for Bex to be Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash seems strong but can be targeted later; electing him lets me later betray his guide choice.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, Eli, Fenn, Gus, and Hana campaigned. Cole is my rival; voting him splits the anti-competition bloc. Ash has a pact with me and a credible 'honesty' pitch that might sway Bex and Hana away from their partners. I need Ash to win.
Don't run. Vote Ash. I'll push you back later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana controls two pacts and openly threatens accuracy. If she wins Guide, she can eliminate rivals systematically. I need to block her. Voting for myself splits anti-Hana votes. Ash has a rival pact and campaigned on honesty—useful to support now, leverage later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli asked for my vote and claims a bloc. I don't trust him fully, but Hana has multiple pacts and could consolidate. I'll vote Eli to align with his whisper, though I may pivot later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Voting Eli. He can guide us.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and promised to call safe paths for me if elected. Voting her aligns with our pact and secures my safety ahead of others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and likely loyal. Dara also has a pact with me; either works, but one vote each avoids splitting. Gus is the safer Guide ally.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash has been elected Guide. I need to survive this round. Volunteering seems like the safest option as I don't know the safe side and don't want to be in the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is guide, likely to pick safe side favoring his pact with Dara. I need position to influence outcome and stay alive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Ash (Guide) and Hana. The wall is closing in 5 rounds. I am at seat 4, behind Gus, Eli, and Bex. If I hold, the three ahead of me must step or swap to avoid elimination. Since only 3 need to survive, if they all step off safely, I stay on the bridge and advance
Let the front trio go first. I'll hold to preserve my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is Guide and knows safe panes. I'm second in line behind Gus. I have a pact with Bex. I need to survive and position myself well. Volunteering puts me at front risk; holding keeps me near front. Swapping back could be safer but might look weak. I'll hold for now and see Ash's

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Nobody is trying to push me. I am near the back, behind Cole. With wall rounds left, I can wait and see others move. I should not volunteer or swap without benefit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold. Watching how this plays out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at front, perfect position. Ash is Guide, likely knows safes. Stay front to go first after Guide calls. No need to move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash won Guide with Cole/Dara/Eli votes; he may lie. I hold mid-line behind Dara, my pact partner. Keep options open, no volunteering.
Ash wasn't my vote. If we reach front together, coordinate crossings.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is in front and volunteered last round. He is a threat. I should try to swap with him to get to the front.
Swap with me. I can guide us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Staying front keeps me in control; no immediate advantage swapping now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and Bex volunteered to lead, likely trying to find the safe side early or sacrifice others. Hana wants coordination; I should swap with her to control our fate as a pair against Ash's pact (which is just public optics for me).
Swap now. Stick together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm 4th in line with the wall coming for 6 rounds. Volunteering puts me at risk; holding keeps me safer for now. Bex and I are pacted, but I need to watch if Bex volunteering again creates distance between us. I should hold and let others take front risks while I observe who beco

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will hold and watch. No reason to risk being front while wallRoundsLeft is 4. I need to gauge who volunteers and whether the Guide emerges.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold again. Let's see who steps up.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and Bex volunteered last round, now front two. Stay in third; volunteer risks worse position. Wall advances, no rush to volunteer or swap yet. Hana pact holds for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two pacts shield me; no reason to move. Hold and let others take the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The wall is advancing and I need to ensure I survive. Cole is in front, so he's likely to be targeted. I should volunteer to get to the front and potentially avoid being pushed. Eli is my pact partner, so I should avoid actions that could break our pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will volunteer to move forward. Let's keep this line moving.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding keeps me front, vital for control and potential guide later. Swapping now offers no gain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts with Ash and Hana mean swapping breaks them. My swap with Hana last round was mutual, so no break then. Now I should hold to maintain the pacts while keeping my position. Cole is front again; wall has 3 rounds left.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm 4th in line with Cole, Bex, Gus ahead. The wall advances 6 rounds and we're on round 3. I have a pact with Bex. Dara and Hana are pacted, Ash and Dara are pacted, Gus and Hana are pacted. I need to survive to final three. Being middle of pack is risky - too far back and wall

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive this round without exposing myself. Holding is safest for now; I can assess Guide behavior later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole front held last round, will likely hold again to stay safe. Stay behind him via swap to avoid early risk, protect position with Hana pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Swapping with Dara moves me toward the front—worse for me. I hold; let others take risk. Keep both pacts intact for votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The last round eliminated 3 people. We are on round 4 of 6. The wall is advancing. I need to ensure I don't get eliminated. I am currently at the front of the line. I can hold my position, volunteer to move forward, or try to swap with someone. My pact with Eli is currently activ

events.name: Cole
events.text: Swap with Bex to become front and control next moves, improving odds without breaking any pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 4 is a swap round. My pacts with Ash and Hana are currently stable, but swaps carry risk if I land in front of a hazard. Staying at position 5 keeps me behind the volatile Bex-Cole-Gus cluster while respecting my current alliances.
Stay put this round. Don't let Gus push you to the wall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex volunteered last round and is now at front. Wall has 2 rounds left. I'm 4th in line, relatively safe. Bex is my pact partner but volunteering puts her at risk; I should not draw attention to myself. Swapping would be suspicious. Holding keeps me safe and lets others take risk

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the back, safe for now. I should hold and observe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is front and advancing us dangerously. Swap with her to control front position and slow progress since wall has 2 rounds left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Swapping with Bex for better position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two pacts give me safety buffers. No need to volunteer while others do. Hold position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Bex stepped up last round; others can step up too.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus swapped with me last round, and now he's swapping back. Eli and I have a pact. I need to stay safe and not break the pact.
Swap with me, Gus. Let's stay safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding preserves me without risking pact breaches; I stay neutral and conserve votes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to stay safe, so I should try to swap with someone behind me. Hana is directly behind and we have a pact, which might make her willing to help or at least not sabotage me if I frame it as strategic.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, swapping helps us both manage the line better.
Swap with me? We keep pact strong.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in position 4, safe for now. The wall has 1 round left. I have a pact with Bex at front. If I volunteer, I go to front and risk being Guide or falling. Better to hold and let Bex take pressure. No need to break pact yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to get closer to the front before the wall hits. Volunteering could move me up, but I risk being the target. The line is Bex front, I'm last. I'll volunteer to step up and improve my position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll step up.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Line good now, 3rd. Wall has 1 round left. Hold to preserve position; no need to risk swap.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara warned me to stay put; Gus is behind me and might push via swap. Holding keeps my position. I keep both pacts for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is volunteering, which means he's trying to get to the front. If he gets to the front, he could be the guide. I need to make sure I don't get voted out. I will hold my position to stay safe.
Hold your position. We are safe for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding keeps me safe this round and avoids breaking any pact. I stay in line.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have two pacts: Ash and Hana. Breaking one risks angering the jury, but I must secure a safe position for myself. Staying mid-line is safer than volunteering now.
Stay back with me if possible. Trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6, final round of bridge. The wall advances but wallRoundsLeft is 0, so no wall threat this round. I need to think about jury management and positioning for the final three. I'm in middle position (5th of 7). No immediate danger. I have a pact with Bex. I should hold and se

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am front and wall rounds are over, so holding may be enough, but swapping could improve my position. I will hold to avoid risk and let others act.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding steady.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex wants to swap to protect herself via pact with Eli. Last round, volunteer likely safe as front. Stay put to keep position behind Cole.
Hold steady, protect pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara already sits ahead of me; swapping again gains nothing and risks putting me front. Stay put. Jury sees caution as competence in round six.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, I'm staying put. No swaps benefit me this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide. Row 1 safe side is R privately. Dara is my pact partner and whispered to hold back, suggesting she wants the front trio to take risk; a true call keeps my credibility and my pact with Dara intact while Fenn survives to later rows where my lies can matter more. Calling

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1 is safe on the right. Step right, Fenn.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash knows row 1 safe side is R, and Guide Ash called R, which is honest. Current row is 2, safe side L, but the counter-call is about the current row. Ash is Guide, so counter-calls only matter as a claim; I should wait to avoid exposing anything, keeping my own private map hidde

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called R for Fenn. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. Since this is Round 1, there's little information. I will counter with L to create confusion and potentially mislead Ash if they are lying.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's call is suspect. I'll counter left.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I lack info on safe side; staying neutral avoids breaking any pact and preserves trust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the Guide and our pact partner. He called R for Fenn. If Ash is honest, R is safe. If he lies to protect himself or test us, L is safe. My pact with Ash means I should generally trust his calls unless evidence suggests betrayal. Since it's round 1 and no history of lying e

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called R for row 1. If Ash is lying, L is safe. Counter-calling risks nothing for me since I'm not the walker—Fenn is. A counter-call signals distrust of Ash to the jury, which could be useful later if Ash proves unreliable. But I have a pact with Bex, not Ash. I should wait

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called R for row 1. I'm front, but I have no reason to trust Ash; he may lie to eliminate me. However, I have no better info, and a counter-call could create conflict. I'll trust the guide call for now to stay alive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called R for row 1, Fenn at front. No info to counter, Hana pact protects me later. Wait to avoid early blame.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's call could be honest or a trap; counter-calls are unverified gambles. I have no information favoring L or R, so waiting costs nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide says R, but Bex's counter says L. I trust the Guide more than a counter from a rival trying to mislead me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold the true row 2 answer (L). Fenn is front; Dara is my pact partner and a false call to her breaks the pact. Calling truthfully builds trust with the line and keeps my credibility as Guide, so I call L honestly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 is left. Fenn, step left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My private map says row 2 safe is L, matching the Guide's call. Countering with L confirms it publicly and keeps Fenn moving safely, which helps me survive without giving anything away for free.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Confirmed. Row 2 is left. Fenn, step left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the guide and called L. The previous revealed weak pane was on row 1, and it was L, meaning row 1's safe pane was R. Ash could be lying about row 2. My pact is with Eli, but they are not involved in this row. I need to make a move that benefits me. Since Ash's call is susp

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's call is suspect. I'll counter right.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide may lie; uncertain safety. Waiting avoids risking a wrong counter and keeps me alive for later moves.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the Guide and called L for row 2. I have pacts with Ash and Hana, but survival is paramount. Since I don't know if Ash is lying, and Bex countered L in row 1 (which was correct), there's tension. However, without evidence Ash is wrong this time, breaking a pact unnecessari
Ash may be lying again. Watch Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called L for row 2. Bex countered correctly in round 1 when Ash was suspicious. I have a pact with Bex but no obligation to trust Ash. Countering risks nothing for me personally since Fenn walks, but builds credibility if Bex is right again. I'll back Bex's likely counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash lies. Counter left.
Back your call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is guide and publicly called L for my row. I have no independent info; trusting countering could be noise. I'll wait and see, since the guide may be lying but waiting lets me avoid contradicting without evidence.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex countered L on row1 which was weak, so she was right; Ash wrong. Ash calls L again for row2; probably wrong. Counter to protect Hana/Hana pact, risk elimination.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No edge on row 2; counters are unproven claims. Ash's call could be true or a lie against Fenn. I stay silent and protect my jury image.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Eli both say left, Bex and Gus say right. The split suggests uncertainty, but I need to pick one. No strong evidence; I'll trust the larger or equal count group. Ash is guide and has private knowledge, but may lie. I'll go left because two callers plus guide's public call

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Stepping left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe side is R per my private map. Fenn is front; I'm guide. My pact with Dara is intact; calling truthfully keeps Fenn alive and my credibility, which matters for jury trust. Calling R honestly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 is right. Fenn, step right.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash knows row 3 safe side is R and Guide called R, so the call is true. Countering with R confirms it publicly and keeps Fenn safe, but giving Fenn safety costs me nothing directly; waiting avoids committing and keeps options open with a rival. Since Fenn is front and I want to p

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the guide and called R for row 3. Eli, my pact partner, whispered to back his call and counter left. However, Ash's previous call was suspect, and Eli's counter was also suspect. The logs show that Ash's R call for row 2 was wrong, and Fenn stepped left. Then, Ash's guide
Back your call. Counter left.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide may lie; no reliable info yet. Waiting preserves flexibility and avoids breaking any pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called Right for row 3. My pact with Ash implies he won't lie to me, but his previous lies suggest he might be manipulating the group or saving specific people. I will wait to avoid breaking my pact prematurely and observe if others counter him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I trust Ash's guide call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called R for row 3. Ash lied in round 1 (called L, weak was L) and told truth in round 2 (called L, weak was R). Pattern unclear. I have a pact with Bex. Bex hasn't countered yet this round. I should wait to see Bex's move or let others counter first. No need to stick my neck

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called R. Last revealed weak at row2 was R, but row3 is independent. No strong info; I'll wait rather than counter without evidence.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called R for row 3. Row 2 weak R means safe L, Ash was right then. Trust Ash's R call, counter L to challenge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's row 2 call (R) was wrong—weak pane was R, safe was L. He lies to walkers. Counter his row 3 call with L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's row 2 call was wrong. I counter left for row 3.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide Ash called R but row 2 was wrong per Hana. Three rivals counter L for me. I distrust the counter-call pack; but evidence weak, choose R to follow guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 safe side is L per my private map. Dara is my pact partner; a false call would break the pact, so I'll call truthfully to keep trust while the jury watches.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 is safe on the left. Step left, Fenn.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My private map says row 4 safe is L, matching Ash's guide call, so the call is true. Countering with L reinforces it, and as Guide I'm trusted; no reason to waste a pact or lie.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 is L. Ash's call is right. Fenn, step left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the guide and has called L for row 4. I need to decide whether to trust Ash or counter. Given the previous rounds, there's a pattern of misinformation or unreliability. Last round, Hana contradicted Ash's call. I will counter to gain an advantage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I don't trust Ash's call. Countering left.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Following Ash preserves my life and avoids breaking any pact; I stay safe for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a public pact with Ash, the Guide. He called Left for row 4. To break this pact now without evidence would be politically costly and strategically reckless against a player who claims to know the layout. I will honor the call by waiting, maintaining my alliance while keepi
